headline: GOLD BOUNCES TO $4,580 OFF $4,500 FLOOR AS IRAN DEAL ADVANCES — MONTHLY LOSS NARROWS
snippet: Gold recovered to $4,580/oz Friday after touching a two-month low of $4,501 earlier in the week, lifted by reports that the US and Iran will extend their ceasefire 60 days and begin nuclear talks. April US inflation — the fastest in three years — reinforces Fed rate-hold expectations into 2027, limiting upside. Gold remains on pace for a 0.8% monthly decline but the $4,500 floor has held on multiple tests, which technicians read as a support signal.

headline: GR SILVER HITS BEST DRILL RESULTS IN COMPANY HISTORY: 45.1m AT 1,623 g/t Ag AT SAN MARCIAL
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV:GRSL) announced company-record drill results May 19 from hole SMS26-04 at San Marcial, Sinaloa, Mexico: 45.1 metres grading 1,623 g/t silver, including a 8.25-metre bonanza intercept at 8,579 g/t Ag — roughly 275 troy ounces per tonne. Two rigs are active in a 20,000-metre step-out campaign, with additional rigs en route. The results confirm a high-grade corridor extending at least 500 metres down dip from surface.

headline: CHINA'S HUAYOU COBALT SNAPS UP GHANA'S EWOYAA LITHIUM PROJECT FOR $210M
snippet: Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt agreed to acquire ASX-listed Atlantic Lithium (ASX:A11) for A$0.354/share — a 26.6% premium — valuing the company at ~A$292M (~US$210M). The deal centres on the Ewoyaa project in Ghana (1.13 million tonnes LCE, JORC-compliant), which secured parliamentary approval of its mining lease in March 2026. Largest shareholder Assore International Holdings has signalled support. Shareholder vote expected November 2026; completion targeted December.

headline: AUSTRALIA ORDERS CHINESE INVESTORS OUT OF RARE EARTH MINER NORTHERN MINERALS IN 14 DAYS
snippet: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers signed orders May 17 requiring six China-linked shareholders to divest stakes in Northern Minerals Ltd within 14 days — the government's second such intervention at the company in two years. Northern Minerals is advancing the Browns Range heavy rare earths project in Western Australia, Australia's highest-grade source of dysprosium and terbium. Shares fell 8% before partially recovering. China's Foreign Ministry objected; it follows a landmark court win last year against a company that breached an earlier divestment order.

headline: NEXGOLD GOLIATH GOLD COMPLEX: 15.21 g/t Au OVER 20m — ONTARIO RESOURCE EXPANSION ON TRACK
snippet: NexGold Mining (TSXV:NEXG) released high-grade gold intercepts May 19 at the Goldlund Deposit within Ontario's Goliath Gold Complex: 15.21 g/t Au over 20.1m, 5.11 g/t over 21.8m, and 4.51 g/t over 21.9m in a 14-hole batch totalling 5,816 metres. Results confirm continuity of Zone 4 mineralization down dip and along strike. The company has completed ~19,000m of a planned 25,000m 2026 infill program. A Canadian Environmental Assessment decision is expected later this year.

headline: TROILUS EXPANDS WEST RIM GOLD DISCOVERY: 2.92 g/t AuEQ OVER 19m OUTSIDE CURRENT RESOURCE
snippet: Troilus Gold (TSX:TLG) announced May 19 that its West Rim zone has returned 2.92 g/t gold equivalent over 19 metres outside the current mineral resource — and within 200 metres of the reserve pit. A secondary hole cut 5.92 g/t Au over 6m at 48m depth. Northern Miner and analysts have flagged the discovery as elevating Troilus's M&A appeal. The company's 2026 program includes a 40,000-metre drill campaign across its 435 km² Athabasca-adjacent land package in Quebec.

headline: META AND MICROSOFT SIGN NUCLEAR SUPPLY DEALS — URANIUM HOLDS NEAR $86.50/LB AT 2-MONTH HIGH
snippet: Uranium futures held near $86.50/lb — a two-month high — as the technology sector's commitment to nuclear power deepens. Meta and Microsoft have both signed agreements for dedicated nuclear capacity to power AI data centers, adding institutional demand signals on top of utility long-term contracting. The Sprott Physical Uranium Trust accumulated 5M+ lbs YTD after a six-month buying pause. Kazatomprom projects a 21-million-pound annual deficit by 2030 as secondary supplies have been largely exhausted.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT CONTROLS SHOW NO SIGN OF EASING AFTER TRUMP-XI SUMMIT
snippet: Benchmark Minerals Intelligence reports that China's rare earth export licensing regime remains largely unchanged following the May 14-15 Trump-Xi summit, despite a White House summary suggesting Beijing had 'agreed to address' US concerns over yttrium, scandium, and neodymium shortages. The updated Export Licensing Catalogue — which added rare-earth compounds, silver, and other materials in January 2026 — continues to restrict up to 13,000 tonnes of annual demand to non-Chinese sources. Ex-China producers and processors are the direct beneficiaries.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE NEARLY DOUBLED IN Q1 2026 AS ENERGY STORAGE FLIPS MARKET INTO DEFICIT
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate nearly doubled to ~$26,278/t in Q1 2026. The driver is structural: battery energy storage demand jumped 71% in 2025, with analysts forecasting another 55% gain in 2026. Guotai Junan projects storage will account for 31% of LCE consumption in 2026 (up from 23% in 2025), flipping what was a 2024 oversupply into a projected 22,000–80,000-tonne deficit. Projects coming online cannot cover the pace of demand growth — a thesis underpinning the Huayou Cobalt / Atlantic Lithium acquisition.

headline: HUDBAY WINS ISS BACKING FOR ARIZONA SONORAN COPPER TAKEOVER AS COPPER M&A HEATS UP
snippet: Independent proxy advisory firm ISS recommended that Arizona Sonoran Copper shareholders vote in favour of Hudbay Minerals' proposed acquisition, with the shareholder vote deadline set for May 7, 2026. The deal consolidates two copper companies with complementary Arizona projects at a time when copper trades near $6.37/lb — up 36% year-over-year — and senior miners are under pressure to replace depleting reserves via M&A rather than greenfield development.

headline: INSTITUTIONAL FORECASTERS STILL SEE $5,000 GOLD — THE CASE HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH IRAN
snippet: GoldSilver.com argues that major bank and asset manager gold forecasts pointing to $5,000+ are built on a structural thesis — dollar debasement, central bank diversification, and geopolitical fragmentation — that is entirely separate from short-term Iran headline risk. The analysis notes gold's bull market has survived April's 3.8% CPI print and two months of rate-hold hawkishness, suggesting the monetary regime is doing the heavy lifting regardless of day-to-day geopolitical noise.
